chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad al-Ju'fi, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I used to frequently complain about my eyes, so I complained of that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said, 'Shall I teach you a supplication for your world and your Hereafter, and a cure for the pain of your eyes?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'You should say at the end of Fajr prayer and the end of Maghrib prayer.'

O Allah, I ask You by the right of Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, send Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and make light in my vision, insight in my religion, conviction in my heart, sincerity in my deeds, safety in my self, expansion in my sustenance, and gratitude to You forever, as long as You keep me alive.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for curing eye pain and gaining spiritual benefits according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication highlights the Imam’s holistic approach to healing, linking physical eye ailments with spiritual clarity (basirah) and sincerity (ikhlas). It is prescribed for recitation after Fajr and Maghrib prayers, emphasizing the intercessory power of the Prophet and his Progeny to secure both worldly well-being and ultimate success in the Hereafter.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Al Ju’fy, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘I used to have a lot of complaints of my eyes, so I complained of that to Abu Abdullahasws. So heasws said, ‘Shall Iasws teach you a supplication for your world and your Hereafter, and would be a cure for the pain of your eyes?’ I said, ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘You should be saying at the end of Al Fajr (Salāt) and the end of Al Maghrib (Salāt),

‘O Allahazwj! I ask Youazwj with the right of Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww upon Youazwj, Send Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, and Make light to be in my vision and the insight to be in my Religion, and the conviction to be in my heart, and the sincerity to be in my deeds, and the safety to be in my self, and the expansion to be in my sustenance, and the gratefulness is to Youazwj, forever, whatever my remaining (life is)’’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad al-Ju’Fi from his father who has said the following:

“I often complained about my eyes and once I mentioned it to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and he said, ‘Should I teach you a supplication that will be for the good of your worldly life and hereafter and a cure for your eye?’ I said, ‘Yes, please do so.’ The Imam said after Maghrib (sunset) prayer say,

‘O Lord, I plead before You through the rights of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad (a.s.) with You to give light to my eyes, understanding in my religion, certainty in my heart, sincerity in my deeds, safety to my soul, increase in my sustenance and gratefulness to You as long as You will keep me (living).”’
